query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Immersing an as‐cast, directionally segregated WTaVTi alloy in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h via liquid‐metal dealloying will yield a composite whose bicontinuous, directionally aligned RHEA–Cu structure forms a robust, approximately 300 nm W-rich interlayer at the RHEA/Cu interfaces. This passivating layer will prevent phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby enhancing temperature‐dependent thermal conductivity and reducing helium-induced swelling under irradiation compared to both the unprocessed precursor and pure W.
generation.material_initial_state: An as‐cast, nominally equiatomic WTaVTi refractory high-entropy alloy with a single-BCC, directionally solidified dendrite–interdendrite structure (W/Ta-rich dendrites and Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels).
generation.intervention: Liquid-metal dealloying by immersing the WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h, thereby selectively extracting Ti from the interdendritic channels.
generation.conditions: The alloy and Cu are vacuum-sealed in silica and reacted at 1200 °C for 96 h. Thermal conductivity is measured from room temperature to approximately 800 °C (with extrapolation above 1000 °C) and He+ irradiation (25 keV up to ~8–8.5 × 10^17 atoms cm−2) is used to assess swelling and blistering behavior.
generation.structural_mediator: A bicontinuous, directionally aligned structure comprising approximately 64 vol.% BCC RHEA ligaments interwoven with 36 vol.% near-pure FCC Cu channels and spontaneously formed ~300 nm W-rich interlayers at the RHEA/Cu interfaces along with minor HCP Ti-rich precipitates.
generation.mechanism: During liquid-metal dealloying, Ti migrates preferentially into Cu due to its negative heat of mixing, leaving behind a RHEA network comprised primarily of W, Ta, and V. Continued extraction of Ti then results in the formation of a W-rich passivating layer at the interface. The formation of aligned Cu channels establishes efficient conductive pathways, while the W-rich interlayer prevents further unwanted interfacial exchange and void formation. Additionally, the complex RHEA lattice resists helium-induced swelling through altered defect dynamics.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the untreated WTaVTi precursor and conventional W–Cu composites, the dealloyed composite is predicted to exhibit substantially higher thermal conductivity at elevated temperatures (above ~650 °C, with superiority over pure W expected beyond 1000 °C) and reduced He-induced swelling and blistering due to the passivating W-rich interlayer and robust RHEA network.
generation.baseline: Performance is compared against the unprocessed WTaVTi precursor alloy, pure W, pure Cu, and reported conventional W–Cu composites; irradiation behavior is further compared with pure W and related compositions like WTa and WTaV.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to composites processed under the specified liquid-metal dealloying conditions (1200 °C/96 h) within a directionally segregated precursor. The thermal improvements are expected primarily at higher temperatures (above ~650 °C) and under low-energy He+ irradiation, with the possibility that differences may not directly extrapolate to neutron irradiation or other high-dose conditions.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainties exist regarding the exact quantitative improvements in thermal conductivity and the precise limits of helium irradiation resistance; extrapolation to service conditions beyond the tested temperature and He+ fluence range should be approached with caution.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare samples of the as-cast WTaVTi precursor and subject one set to the liquid-metal dealloying process (immersed in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h). Characterize both samples using SEM/TEM with EDS to confirm the formation of the directionally aligned structure and the ~300 nm W-rich interlayers. Measure phase constitution using XRD and evaluate thermal conductivity using laser-flash analysis across the target temperature range. Subject samples to 25 keV He+ irradiation up to blistering fluences (~8–8.5 × 10^17 atoms cm−2) and image surface swelling and blister formation using AFM.
measurements: SEM/TEM-EDS for microstructural verification and interlayer formation
Laser-flash analysis for temperature-dependent thermal conductivity
AFM for quantifying post-irradiation swelling and blister/cracking onset
Nanoindentation to assess the mechanical properties of the composite channels
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the dealloyed composite does not exhibit a significantly higher thermal conductivity (particularly at temperatures above ~650 °C), or if interfacial void formation and comparable levels of He-induced swelling/blistering are observed relative to the untreated precursor or pure W, then the hypothesis is falsified.
